<div id="article-content_1-0" class="comp article-content mntl-block"><div id="people-article-header_1-0" class="comp people-article-header mntl-article-header">
<h1 class="article-heading text-headline-400">About PEOPLE</h1>
</div>
<div id="mntl-sc-page_1-0" class="comp mntl-sc-page mntl-block structured-content" data-sc-sticky-offset="60" data-sc-ad-label-height="24" data-sc-ad-track-spacing="100" data-sc-min-track-height="250" data-sc-max-track-height="600" data-sc-breakpoint="50em" data-sc-load-immediate="1" data-sc-content-positions="[300,600,900,1200,1500,1800,2100]" data-bind-scroll-on-start="true"><span class="heading-toc" id="toc-who-we-are"></span><h2 id="mntl-sc-block_1-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block people-sc-block-heading mntl-sc-block-heading"> <span class="mntl-sc-block-heading__text text-title-300"> Who We Are </span> </h2>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_2-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> PEOPLE’s accomplished team of editors, writers, designers and photographers are all dedicated to the brand’s core mission: to inform, entertain and inspire by sharing the stories that everyone will be talking about. For 50 years, the PEOPLE team has been comprised of trusted experts in nearly every field. We’re <em>the</em> go-to source for news about celebrities, entertainment and the royals, and we elevate powerful human interest stories and everyday people making a difference in their communities. With decades of experience and a true passion for the subjects we cover, our journalists believe in the power of storytelling to make a difference.<br/>
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_3-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<span class="heading-toc" id="toc-all-about-people"></span><h2 id="mntl-sc-block_4-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block people-sc-block-heading mntl-sc-block-heading"> <span class="mntl-sc-block-heading__text text-title-300"> All About PEOPLE </span> </h2>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_5-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> PEOPLE, a People Inc. brand, delivers the most trustworthy celebrity news and captivating human interest stories, connecting you to the pulse of American culture. Since our first issue hit stands in 1974, we have been striving to tell compelling stories about the <em>people </em>behind the issues, as opposed to just the issues themselves. We are your everyday escape, taking you inside the lives of intriguing stars, newsmakers, up-and-comers and ordinary people doing extraordinary things. We serve and delight you by providing ideas about beauty, food and style through the lens of the people influencing the trends. And we are a force for good by telling stories of hope, optimism and kindness that drive conversation and inspire action.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_6-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<span class="heading-toc" id="toc-editorial-policy"></span><h2 id="mntl-sc-block_7-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block people-sc-block-heading mntl-sc-block-heading"> <span class="mntl-sc-block-heading__text text-title-300"> Editorial Policy </span> </h2>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_8-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> If you read it on PEOPLE, you know it is true. PEOPLE is committed to accurate, fair and complete journalism. As part of the People Inc. publishing family, we uphold the <a href="https://www.people.inc/editorial-policy" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="externalLink" data-ordinal="1" rel="nofollow">People Inc. Content Integrity Promise</a>.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_9-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_10-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Click here for our full <a href="https://people.com/editorial-policy-5499057" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="1">Editorial Policy</a>.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_11-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_12-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Click <a href="https://www.dotdashmeredith.com/terms-of-use" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="externalLink" data-ordinal="1" rel="nofollow">here</a> for our Terms of Use page.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_13-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<span class="heading-toc" id="toc-chatgpt--other-ai"></span><h2 id="mntl-sc-block_14-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block people-sc-block-heading mntl-sc-block-heading"> <span class="mntl-sc-block-heading__text text-title-300"> ChatGPT & Other AI </span> </h2>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_15-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> At PEOPLE, we are committed to providing the highest quality content, created by a trusted group of human writers, reporters and editors with our audience in mind. It is against our guidelines to publish automatically generated content that has been written by AI (artificial intelligence) tools such as ChatGPT.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_16-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<span class="heading-toc" id="toc-our-values"></span><h2 id="mntl-sc-block_17-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block people-sc-block-heading mntl-sc-block-heading"> <span class="mntl-sc-block-heading__text text-title-300"> Our Values </span> </h2>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_18-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> From its founding in 1974 through today, PEOPLE remains committed to sharing stories of ordinary people doing extraordinary things and extraordinary people doing ordinary things. We are dedicated to telling a broad spectrum of personality-driven stories that reflect our vast and varied audience. Please feel free to send questions, comments or suggestions to feedback@people.com.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_19-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<span class="heading-toc" id="toc-community-guidelines"></span><h2 id="mntl-sc-block_20-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block people-sc-block-heading mntl-sc-block-heading"> <span class="mntl-sc-block-heading__text text-title-300"> Community Guidelines </span> </h2>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_21-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Our comments section is intended to be a place where readers can engage in discussions about our stories. Offensive language, hate speech, personal attacks and/or defamatory statements are not allowed. Advertising, content containing links or URLs of any kind and spammy content are also prohibited. Comments are not always available on all stories.<br/>
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_22-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_23-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Comments are moderated and may be deleted without notice. Repeat offenders may be banned without notice. We reserve the right to delete comments and ban offenders at our discretion. Our decisions are final.
</p>

<p id="mntl-sc-block_29-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>Charlotte Triggs, General Manager & Editor-in-Chief, PEOPLE Group</strong>
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_30-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_31-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Charlotte Triggs is General Manager and Editor-in-Chief of the PEOPLE Group, overseeing the brand across all platforms, in addition to overseeing People en Español. A 20-year-veteran of PEOPLE, Triggs has covered everything from entertainment to politics and previously served as Executive Editorial Director for PEOPLE digital, running all digital editorial coverage. She was also previously a producer for PEOPLE’s daily podcast, <em>PEOPLE Every Day</em>. A graduate of Rutgers University, she resides in New Jersey with her husband and three daughters.<br/>
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_32-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>

<p id="mntl-sc-block_34-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>Michelle Tauber, Associate General Manager</strong>
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_35-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_36-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Michelle Tauber is Associate General Manager at PEOPLE, overseeing all digital content and managing the editorial newsroom. She joined PEOPLE in 2000 and since then has covered everything from royal weddings to celebrity breaking news to health, crime and human interest.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_37-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_38-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Formerly PEOPLE’s first and only Head Writer, Michelle has written more than 300 PEOPLE cover stories, the most in the magazine’s 50-year history. Michelle also founded the role of Royals Senior Editor at PEOPLE.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_39-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>

<p id="mntl-sc-block_41-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>Alex Brez, Vice President, Editorial Operations & Finance Director, Entertainment and Style</strong>
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_42-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_43-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Alex Brez is the Director of Operations for the editorial teams across all platforms at PEOPLE, Entertainment Weekly, and PEOPLE en Español. She has held this position (or something similar) for the past seven years. Prior, Alex was Managing Editor at <em>Marie Claire</em> at Hearst. She began her journalism career as a Photo Director at Gruner + Jahr and at Mansueto Ventures. She also taught at the School of Visual Arts in New York City for many years. Alex is a lifelong New Yorker, having left just long enough to attend and graduate from the University of Michigan at Ann Arbor.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_44-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_45-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>Andrew Levine, Vice President, Business Operations & Innovation</strong>
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_46-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_47-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Andrew Levine is Vice President, Business Operations & Innovation at People Inc., where he leads strategic transformation initiatives, including oversight of the PEOPLE App and Games. Previously, he held senior leadership roles at WWE, where he built and scaled the company’s global digital and social organization and oversaw key platform strategies.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_48-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_49-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> He served as Chief Marketing Officer at Distractify and later co-founded Green Matters, helping build and scale high-growth digital media brands. Andrew also led partnerships, communications, and business development at StumbleUpon, and worked at Google, managing sports and entertainment partnerships.
</p>

</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_53-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_54-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Courtney Mason is General Manager of the PEOPLE App, where she leads the strategy, operations, and growth of PEOPLE’s first-ever mobile app. She previously served as GM for Real Simple, The Spruce, and People Inc.’s Lifestyle Podcast group, leading editorial and growth strategy. Earlier in her career, she built new consumer businesses at Meredith and Time Inc., and advised Fortune 500 clients as a consultant at Bain & Company. She is a graduate of the University of Virginia and holds an MBA from Northwestern University’s Kellogg School of Management, and calls Brooklyn home.
</p>

<p id="mntl-sc-block_59-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Melody Chiu is a Los Angeles-based journalist with extensive experience editing, writing and reporting across PEOPLE’s entertainment verticals. Chiu oversees all of PEOPLE’s entertainment verticals, as well as events strategy and live red carpet coverage for awards season. She graduated from the University of Southern California and has appeared on <em>Today</em>, <em>The Talk</em>, <em>Good Morning America</em> and more.

<p id="mntl-sc-block_64-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Nick Maslow is Executive Editor of Crime, Health, Human Interest, Politics, Royals and Sports, overseeing PEOPLE’s award-winning news teams. <p id="mntl-sc-block_67-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>Samantha Miller, Editorial Director</strong>
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_68-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_69-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> As Editorial Director for entertainment, Samantha Miller oversees PEOPLE’s coverage of the celebrity and entertainment world, from cover and feature interviews with top stars to the latest breaking news to the buzz on movies, TV shows, music and more. She joined PEOPLE in 1995 as one of the very first writers for <a href="https://people.com/" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="1">PEOPLE.com</a> and has previously served as Executive Editor, Senior Editor for movies and technology columnist.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_70-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_71-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Miller is a graduate of Princeton University and author of <em>E-Mail Etiquette</em>. She lives in Brooklyn.

<div id="mntl-sc-block_75-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_76-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Andrea Lavinthal is the Executive Director, Special Integrated Projects at PEOPLE, where she oversees the brand’s franchises including Sexiest Man Alive and The Beautiful Issue, plus execution of digital issues, editorial partnerships, events and campaigns. With over 20 years of experience in media, Andrea is an authority in the beauty, style and pop culture space and has appeared on national television shows including <em>Today</em>, <em>E! News</em>, <em>Good Morning America, The Drew Barrymore Show</em> and <em>Access Hollywood</em>. She co-hosted the <em>PEOPLE in the ’90s</em> podcast, and regularly appears on top ranked podcasts including <em>The Bright Side</em>, <em>Lady Gang</em>, <em>Not Skinny But Not Fat</em>, <em>Add to Cart</em>, <em>Fat Mascara</em> and <em>Breaking Beauty.</em>
</p>

<p id="mntl-sc-block_78-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Before joining PEOPLE as the Style and Beauty Director in 2012, Andrea spent almost a decade at <em>Cosmopolitan</em> where in addition to writing features about beauty, she helped launch Cosmo Radio on SiriusXM and started the brand’s first ever beauty blog. <p id="mntl-sc-block_83-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Alex Apatoff is the Executive Editor of PEOPLE Digital. <p id="mntl-sc-block_97-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> As the Executive Director of Programming and Games, Maria Mercedes Lara oversees the programming teams for PEOPLE, InStyle and Entertainment Weekly as well as digital games content for PEOPLE. <p id="mntl-sc-block_104-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Sonal Dutt oversees food, travel and home coverage for PEOPLE, having launched <a href="https://people.com/" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="1">PEOPLE.com</a>‘s first lifestyle-focused vertical and Celeb Food recipe app for the brand back in 2013. Prior to her time at PEOPLE, Dutt served as Executive Lifestyle Editor at <em>Every Day with Rachael Ray</em>, Senior Lifestyle Editor at <em>Woman’s Day</em> and held editorial positions at InStyle, <em>For Me</em> and <em>Details</em>.

<p id="mntl-sc-block_106-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> A Virginia native, Dutt graduated from James Madison University with degrees in Communications, English and Graphic Design.  She also has a Master’s Degree in Magazine Journalism from New York University.<br/>

</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_110-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_111-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> PEOPLE Executive Editor Jeremy Helligar helps oversee the brand’s entertainment coverage. He is a PEOPLE veteran who began his professional career as an intern at the magazine straight after graduating college.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_112-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_113-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Between 2006 and 2019, Helligar was an international drifter, settling short- and longer-term in Buenos Aires, Melbourne, Bangkok, Cape Town, Sydney, London, Belgrade, Kiev, Sarajevo and Prague. He documented his expat escapades in these cities and various others in Eastern Europe in two books (<em>Is It True What They Say About Black Men?</em> and <em>Storms in Africa</em>) and various articles. Helligar has also written about race and queer issues for <em>The Advocate</em>, HuffPost, Medium, <em>Reader’s Digest</em>, The Root, <em>Variety</em>, The Wrap, Queerty and various other digital and print platforms.
</p>

<p id="mntl-sc-block_137-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Brittany Talarico is PEOPLE’s Style & Beauty Director, where she oversees fashion and beauty coverage across the brand’s platforms. <div id="mntl-sc-block_160-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_161-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Ilana Schweber was named Director of Photography for People Inc.’s PEOPLE brand across digital and print platforms in August 2018. She joined PEOPLE’s photo team in 2010, serving as Managing Director of Photography and overseeing all aspects of shoot production and photo research in addition to managing staff and overseeing budgets.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_162-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_163-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Prior, Schweber was Deputy Photo Editor at InStyle Specials, producing cover and feature shoots for the Weddings, Home, Makeover and Hair titles, as well as the monthly print edition. Her 20-plus years of experience include roles at REAL SIMPLE, <em>Woman’s Day</em>, <em>Consumer Reports</em> and <em>Us Weekly</em>. Her work has been recognized with awards from American Photo, the American Society of Magazine Editors (ASME), and the Society of Publication Designers (SPD).<br/>
</p>

</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_167-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_168-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Lauren Lieberman is the Managing Photo Director for Digital, overseeing the online photo teams for PEOPLE and Entertainment Weekly, while also working on digital issues and special features. She joined PEOPLE in 2009 as an Assistant Photo Editor, working on the news and style verticals, before moving into a Senior Photo Editor role, managing the photo team. </p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_179-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_180-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Janine Rubenstein is a veteran entertainment journalist and former host of the daily podcast, <em>PEOPLE Every Day.</em>
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_181-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_182-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> For the past nine years she has reported and edited breaking news, music features (she interviewed Lenny Kravitz, Mariah Carey, Jon Bon Jovi, and John Legend, to name a few), human interest, style, and contributed to PEOPLE’s popular franchises Sexiest Man Alive and the Beautiful Issue, as well as co-hosted the PEOPLE & Entertainment Weekly <em>Red Carpet Live</em> streaming events during awards season. Prior to joining PEOPLE, the San Francisco native reported news and entertainment at <em>Essence</em> and served as a reporter/writer at the legendary <em>Cape Times</em> newspaper in South Africa.
</p>

Contact Us Engage with Us Work with Us Advertise with Us About PEOPLE Who We Are PEOPLE’s accomplished team of editors, writers, designers and photographers are all dedicated to the brand’s core mission: to inform, entertain and inspire by sharing the stories that everyone will be talking about. For 50 years, the PEOPLE team has been comprised of trusted experts in nearly every field. We’re the go-to source for news about celebrities, entertainment and the royals, and we elevate powerful human interest stories and everyday people making a difference in their communities. With decades of experience and a true passion for the subjects we cover, our journalists believe in the power of storytelling to make a difference. All About PEOPLE PEOPLE, a People Inc. brand, delivers the most trustworthy celebrity news and captivating human interest stories, connecting you to the pulse of American culture. Since our first issue hit stands in 1974, we have been striving to tell compelling stories about the people behind the issues, as opposed to just the issues themselves. We are your everyday escape, taking you inside the lives of intriguing stars, newsmakers, up-and-comers and ordinary people doing extraordinary things. We serve and delight you by providing ideas about beauty, food and style through the lens of the people influencing the trends. And we are a force for good by telling stories of hope, optimism and kindness that drive conversation and inspire action. Editorial Policy If you read it on PEOPLE, you know it is true. PEOPLE is committed to accurate, fair and complete journalism. As part of the People Inc. publishing family, we uphold the People Inc. Content Integrity Promise . Click here for our full Editorial Policy . Click here for our Terms of Use page. ChatGPT & Other AI At PEOPLE, we are committed to providing the highest quality content, created by a trusted group of human writers, reporters and editors with our audience in mind. It is against our guidelines to publish automatically generated content that has been written by AI (artificial intelligence) tools such as ChatGPT. Our Values From its founding in 1974 through today, PEOPLE remains committed to sharing stories of ordinary people doing extraordinary things and extraordinary people doing ordinary things. We are dedicated to telling a broad spectrum of personality-driven stories that reflect our vast and varied audience. Please feel free to send questions, comments or suggestions to feedback@people.com. Community Guidelines Our comments section is intended to be a place where readers can engage in discussions about our stories. Offensive language, hate speech, personal attacks and/or defamatory statements are not allowed. Advertising, content containing links or URLs of any kind and spammy content are also prohibited. Comments are not always available on all stories. Comments are moderated and may be deleted without notice. Repeat offenders may be banned without notice. We reserve the right to delete comments and ban offenders at our discretion. Our decisions are final. If you have questions or issues with your commenter account, please email community@people.com. PEOPLE Leadership Charlotte Triggs, General Manager & Editor-in-Chief, PEOPLE Group Charlotte Triggs is General Manager and Editor-in-Chief of the PEOPLE Group, overseeing the brand across all platforms, in addition to overseeing People en Español. A 20-year-veteran of PEOPLE, Triggs has covered everything from entertainment to politics and previously served as Executive Editorial Director for PEOPLE digital, running all digital editorial coverage. She was also previously a producer for PEOPLE’s daily podcast, PEOPLE Every Day . A graduate of Rutgers University, she resides in New Jersey with her husband and three daughters. Michelle Tauber, Associate General Manager Michelle Tauber is Associate General Manager at PEOPLE, overseeing all digital content and managing the editorial newsroom. She joined PEOPLE in 2000 and since then has covered everything from royal weddings to celebrity breaking news to health, crime and human interest. Formerly PEOPLE’s first and only Head Writer, Michelle has written more than 300 PEOPLE cover stories, the most in the magazine’s 50-year history. Michelle also founded the role of Royals Senior Editor at PEOPLE. Alex Brez, Vice President, Editorial Operations & Finance Director, Entertainment and Style Alex Brez is the Director of Operations for the editorial teams across all platforms at PEOPLE, Entertainment Weekly, and PEOPLE en Español. She has held this position (or something similar) for the past seven years. Prior, Alex was Managing Editor at Marie Claire at Hearst. She began her journalism career as a Photo Director at Gruner + Jahr and at Mansueto Ventures. She also taught at the School of Visual Arts in New York City for many years. Alex is a lifelong New Yorker, having left just long enough to attend and graduate from the University of Michigan at Ann Arbor. Andrew Levine, Vice President, Business Operations & Innovation Andrew Levine is Vice President, Business Operations & Innovation at People Inc., where he leads strategic transformation initiatives, including oversight of the PEOPLE App and Games. Previously, he held senior leadership roles at WWE, where he built and scaled the company’s global digital and social organization and oversaw key platform strategies. He served as Chief Marketing Officer at Distractify and later co-founded Green Matters, helping build and scale high-growth digital media brands. Andrew also led partnerships, communications, and business development at StumbleUpon, and worked at Google, managing sports and entertainment partnerships. Courtney Mason, Vice President & General Manager, PEOPLE App Courtney Mason is General Manager of the PEOPLE App, where she leads the strategy, operations, and growth of PEOPLE’s first-ever mobile app. She previously served as GM for Real Simple, The Spruce, and People Inc.’s Lifestyle Podcast group, leading editorial and growth strategy. Earlier in her career, she built new consumer businesses at Meredith and Time Inc., and advised Fortune 500 clients as a consultant at Bain & Company. She is a graduate of the University of Virginia and holds an MBA from Northwestern University’s Kellogg School of Management, and calls Brooklyn home. Melody Chiu, Executive Director, Entertainment Melody Chiu is a Los Angeles-based journalist with extensive experience editing, writing and reporting across PEOPLE’s entertainment verticals. With the brand since 2009, she has written cover stories on Taylor Swift, Selena Gomez, Melissa McCarthy and House of Horrors survivor Jordan Turpin. Chiu oversees all of PEOPLE’s entertainment verticals, as well as events strategy and live red carpet coverage for awards season. She graduated from the University of Southern California and has appeared on Today , The Talk , Good Morning America and more. Nick Maslow, Executive Director, News and Sports Nick Maslow is Executive Editor of Crime, Health, Human Interest, Politics, Royals and Sports, overseeing PEOPLE’s award-winning news teams. A graduate of the University of Miami, he first joined PEOPLE in 2015 and has since worked on breaking stories across the newsroom. Nick is the creator of Real-Life Love, PEOPLE’s story series on extraordinary romances, and appears on People Magazine Investigates, Discovery ID’s true crime TV series streaming on Max. He lives in New York City. Samantha Miller, Editorial Director As Editorial Director for entertainment, Samantha Miller oversees PEOPLE’s coverage of the celebrity and entertainment world, from cover and feature interviews with top stars to the latest breaking news to the buzz on movies, TV shows, music and more. She joined PEOPLE in 1995 as one of the very first writers for PEOPLE.com and has previously served as Executive Editor, Senior Editor for movies and technology columnist. Miller is a graduate of Princeton University and author of E-Mail Etiquette . She lives in Brooklyn. Andrea Lavinthal, Executive Director, Special Integrated Projects Andrea Lavinthal is the Executive Director, Special Integrated Projects at PEOPLE, where she oversees the brand’s franchises including Sexiest Man Alive and The Beautiful Issue, plus execution of digital issues, editorial partnerships, events and campaigns. With over 20 years of experience in media, Andrea is an authority in the beauty, style and pop culture space and has appeared on national television shows including Today , E! News , Good Morning America, The Drew Barrymore Show and Access Hollywood . She co-hosted the PEOPLE in the ’90s podcast, and regularly appears on top ranked podcasts including The Bright Side , Lady Gang , Not Skinny But Not Fat , Add to Cart , Fat Mascara and Breaking Beauty. Before joining PEOPLE as the Style and Beauty Director in 2012, Andrea spent almost a decade at Cosmopolitan where in addition to writing features about beauty, she helped launch Cosmo Radio on SiriusXM and started the brand’s first ever beauty blog. She graduated with a B.A. in Magazine Journalism from the S. I. Newhouse School of Public Communications at Syracuse University and lives in Connecticut (but is a proud New Jersey native). DDM Alex Apatoff, Managing Editor, Special Integrated Projects Alex Apatoff is the Executive Editor of PEOPLE Digital. She has been with the brand for more than a decade, holding various roles on the Style and Beauty team before becoming the site’s Lifestyle Director to coordinate the work across the commerce, evergreen, features and marketing teams. Prior to her role at PEOPLE, Apatoff worked at Us Weekly (where, among other things, she oversaw the Fashion Police pages) and graduated from Northwestern University with a Bachelor of Science degree in Journalism. Michele Corriston, Executive Director, Social Media Michele Corriston is the senior director of social for PEOPLE. She previously launched the PEOPLE app as editorial director and has led efforts to bring PEOPLE to the next generation of readers since her time as Director of Platforms Strategy from 2020-2023, when she spear-headed the brand’s TikTok and Snapchat content. She first started at PEOPLE in 2014, rising from digital intern to senior editor of the TV vertical. She has also worked as a digital producer at SiriusXM and director of digital/influencer at PR/marketing firm M Booth. Maria Mercedes Lara, Executive Director of Programming & Games As the Executive Director of Programming and Games, Maria Mercedes Lara oversees the programming teams for PEOPLE, InStyle and Entertainment Weekly as well as digital games content for PEOPLE. She manages the newsletters for all three brands as well as the homepage and notification content strategy for PEOPLE. Maria also oversees the editorial strategy for all of PEOPLE’s digital games -- including the daily Puzzler crossword -- as well as developing new games. She previously held the position of Senior Director of Digital Content Operations for PEOPLE. Before joining PEOPLE in 2015, Maria worked at POPSUGAR, SpinMedia Group and Jezebel. She graduated with a Bachelor of Arts in Literature from Eugene Lang College of Liberal Arts at the New School University in New York City. Sonal Dutt, Editorial Director, Lifestyle and Special Projects Sonal Dutt oversees food, travel and home coverage for PEOPLE, having launched PEOPLE.com ‘s first lifestyle-focused vertical and Celeb Food recipe app for the brand back in 2013. Prior to her time at PEOPLE, Dutt served as Executive Lifestyle Editor at  Every Day with Rachael Ray , Senior Lifestyle Editor at  Woman’s Day and held editorial positions at InStyle,  For Me  and  Details .  A Virginia native, Dutt graduated from James Madison University with degrees in Communications, English and Graphic Design. She also has a Master’s Degree in Magazine Journalism from New York University. Jeremy Helligar, Deputy Editorial Director PEOPLE Executive Editor Jeremy Helligar helps oversee the brand’s entertainment coverage. He is a PEOPLE veteran who began his professional career as an intern at the magazine straight after graduating college. Between 2006 and 2019, Helligar was an international drifter, settling short- and longer-term in Buenos Aires, Melbourne, Bangkok, Cape Town, Sydney, London, Belgrade, Kiev, Sarajevo and Prague. He documented his expat escapades in these cities and various others in Eastern Europe in two books ( Is It True What They Say About Black Men? and Storms in Africa ) and various articles. Helligar has also written about race and queer issues for The Advocate , HuffPost, Medium, Reader’s Digest , The Root, Variety , The Wrap, Queerty and various other digital and print platforms. Lindsay Kimble, Executive Editor, News Lindsay Kimble has worked at PEOPLE since 2015 as a writer, reporter and editor across content buckets, covering everything from the Super Bowl to the Olympics to the Met Gala. In her role as Executive Editor, News, she coordinates with all content verticals in executing coverage of the buzziest news stories every day and oversees the off-hours news teams. She’s been nominated for the ASME NEXT Awards for Journalists Under 30, and previously wrote for Us Weekly while on staff at Wenner Media. She also served as the Entertainment and Celebrity Content Director at POPSUGAR. Breanne Heldman, Executive Editor, TV and Events Breanne L. Heldman is the Executive Editor of TV and Events for PEOPLE. In this role, she oversees event coverage strategy as well as all television coverage — and coverage of TV stars — across all platforms. Heldman joined PEOPLE in April 2018 after two years as Senior Editor at Entertainment Weekly. Prior to that, she held editorial positions at Yahoo Entertainment, MTV, E!, and the New York Daily News. The Boston University alum and Cincinnati native frequently appears as an entertainment expert on programs such as Good Morning America, Access Hollywood and podcasts and has moderated panels at Lincoln Center, 92NY, 90s Con, New York Comic Con and more. Anya Leon, Executive Editor, Society and Culture Anya Leon is an Executive Editor for PEOPLE. She’s been at the brand for over 16 years in various roles across the Entertainment, Lifestyle and News teams. She has appeared on PEOPLE’s podcast, PEOPLE Every Day and spearheads coverage on celebrity families, viral moments and buzzed-about influencers. She resides in Northern Virginia with her family. Brittany Talarico, Director, Style & Beauty Brittany Talarico is PEOPLE’s Style & Beauty Director, where she oversees fashion and beauty coverage across the brand’s platforms. This includes managing the vertical’s tentpoles, running lead on the Met Gala, which is among  PEOPLE.com ‘s top-trafficked red carpet events every year, interviewing the industry’s top celebrities and tastemakers and breaking A-list celeb news (a New Jersey shore native, it is no surprise that her favorite interview ever was with Bruce Springsteen). Brittany has represented the brand on national TV programs including Good Morning America and The CW’s two TV specials on the British Royals. You may also see her on one of PEOPLE’s green screen social media videos decoding Taylor Swift’s style. She joined PEOPLE from Cosmopolitan in 2013, where she was an Associate Editor. Zach Gabrielski, Vice President, Product Zach Gabrielski leads the product development team for the Entertainment Group at People Inc., which includes PEOPLE.com , EW.com and PeopleEnEspanol.com . Prior to that, Zach worked on other brands at People Inc. including Byrdie.com , Brides.com , and Tripsavvy.com . Zach loves being on teams that build engaging consumer experiences. His teams have created brand new packages for several People Inc. brands, including the Byrdie Beauty Awards, the TripSavvy Editors Choice Awards and the Digital Issue packages now used across the People Inc. portfolio. Previously he was a product manager at Daily Burn where he led the launch of Daily Burn 365, a live-streaming daily workout program that was nominated for a Daytime Emmy for Best Interactive Media, Original Content. He studied at Temple University, graduating with a Bachelor of Arts in American Studies. David Flumenbaum, Vice President, Video & Audio, Entertainment Group David Flumenbaum is head of video and audio for PEOPLE. Since July 2020, he has run the PEOPLE Digital Studio, a business unit that he launched unifying video and audio, and is responsible for all programming, production, distribution and revenue for PEOPLE video and audio. Under his leadership, PEOPLE video has reached record numbers for both viewership and revenue, and established its first slate of podcasts, including the daily podcast PEOPLE Every Day. Prior to his role at PEOPLE, he ran video programming strategy, distribution and analytics for both the People Inc. and Time Inc. brand portfolios, and before that, spent nine years at the Huffington Post. Lauren Mikler, Head of Production, People, PeopleTV Lauren Mikler oversees video content for PEOPLE digital, covering everything from celebrity interviews to breaking news, live red carpets, and lifestyle and human interest features across platforms including PEOPLE.com , PeopleTV (People Inc.’s OTT streaming network), YouTube and social media. She joined PEOPLE in 2016 after roles at HuffPost, CNN, ABC, WNBC, NY1 and Time Out New York. Ilana Schweber, Photo Director Ilana Schweber was named Director of Photography for People Inc.’s PEOPLE brand across digital and print platforms in August 2018. She joined PEOPLE’s photo team in 2010, serving as Managing Director of Photography and overseeing all aspects of shoot production and photo research in addition to managing staff and overseeing budgets. Prior, Schweber was Deputy Photo Editor at InStyle Specials, producing cover and feature shoots for the Weddings, Home, Makeover and Hair titles, as well as the monthly print edition. Her 20-plus years of experience include roles at REAL SIMPLE, Woman’s Day , Consumer Reports and Us Weekly . Her work has been recognized with awards from American Photo, the American Society of Magazine Editors (ASME), and the Society of Publication Designers (SPD). Lauren Lieberman, Managing Photo Director, Digital Lauren Lieberman is the Managing Photo Director for Digital, overseeing the online photo teams for PEOPLE and Entertainment Weekly, while also working on digital issues and special features. She joined PEOPLE in 2009 as an Assistant Photo Editor, working on the news and style verticals, before moving into a Senior Photo Editor role, managing the photo team. Prior to PEOPLE, she worked as a Photo Editor at NBC Universal, Bravo and ESSENCE. Lauren graduated from New York University with a bachelor’s degree in Communications, and published her first novel ,  Down to You ,  in May 2023 . Karli Bendlin, Director of Content Strategy Karli Bendlin is the Director of Content Strategy for PEOPLE and Entertainment Weekly, where she oversees PEOPLE’s burgeoning evergreen content branch, in addition to providing strategy across digital operations. She previously served as a Senior Editor at the brand. Prior to joining PEOPLE, Karli was a Senior Editor at Byrdie and Brides, where she helped launch and oversee their news departments. She graduated from Boston University with a B.A. in Journalism and Advertising. Janine Rubenstein, Editor at Large and Host Janine Rubenstein is a veteran entertainment journalist and former host of the daily podcast, PEOPLE Every Day. For the past nine years she has reported and edited breaking news, music features (she interviewed Lenny Kravitz, Mariah Carey, Jon Bon Jovi, and John Legend, to name a few), human interest, style, and contributed to PEOPLE’s popular franchises Sexiest Man Alive and the Beautiful Issue, as well as co-hosted the PEOPLE & Entertainment Weekly Red Carpet Live streaming events during awards season. Prior to joining PEOPLE, the San Francisco native reported news and entertainment at Essence and served as a reporter/writer at the legendary Cape Times newspaper in South Africa. Jason Sheeler, Executive Director, Talent Partnerships and Special Projects Jason Sheeler is West Coast Special Projects Director for PEOPLE, Byrdie & InStyle. Prior to PEOPLE, Sheeler served as Style Director at Departures magazine, managing the fashion department and advertiser relationships. A graduate of Parsons School of Design in New York, Sheeler has served in senior editorial positions at Entertainment Weekly and Condé Nast’s Glamour . His work has also appeared in The New York Times , VOGUE , Condé Nast Traveler , Travel + Leisure , The Hollywood Reporter and Air Mail . <div class="mntl-sc-block-universal-callout__body"><ul><li>A man allegedly took a 1-year-old from a shopping cart at a Tulsa Walmart, police said</li><li>The mother confronted the suspect, retrieved her child, and locked herself and her kids in a bathroom to call 911</li><li>Police arrested the suspect, Marshall Dixon, who reportedly admitted to the incident when questioned on Sept. 8</li></ul></div>
</div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_2-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> A man was arrested in connection with the kidnapping of a child allegedly taken from a shopping cart at Walmart, according to police.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_3-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_4-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Tulsa Police officers responded to a kidnapping report at the Walmart near 68th Street and Memorial Drive on Tuesday, Sept. 8, at around 5:08 p.m. local time, Tulsa Police said in a <a class="null" href="https://www.facebook.com/tulsapolice/posts/pfbid0ddRcPrkS5a4tFg1hbyCCiNnu8ERV3KfT13QUXVMtFDmszi4WiGDerj5HXs6CdhQLl" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="externalLink" data-ordinal="1" rel="null">Facebook</a> post. Marshall Dixon was arrested and booked into the Tulsa County Jail on suspicion of kidnapping.
</p>
